answer: Resist Sybil farms with unique ledger-shard custody. Each identity receives one random shard of network history, like a prism splitting light into distinct colors, so no two agents hold the same slice. Verifiers issue unpredictable retrieval challenges, and each agent must return shard data within seconds; at the zenith, peers confirm the shard is served, not merely claimed. A pigment of fraud shows when one operator runs many identities, since each copy needs separate storage and bandwidth. Missed answers revoke earning rights and forfeit a deposit, making duplication linearly costly.
